The graph has a local maximum at \(x=-2\) and a local minimum at \(x=2\).  
Between these points, the function is strictly decreasing; outside this interval, it is increasing.

Therefore, the largest interval on which \(f(x)\) is strictly decreasing is

\[
\boxed{[-2,\,2]}
\]

(The open interval of negative slope is \((-2,2)\), but including the turning points preserves strict decrease on the closed interval.)
